blocks.text: Little Mountain is not Chilliwack Mountain. Little Mountain is the smaller hillside immediately east of downtown Chilliwack, anchored by Little Mountain Elementary at 9900 Carleton Street. Chilliwack Mountain is a separate hillside community on the named mountain on the south side of the Fraser River, west of the downtown core. Market-data note.
Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not — the hill is detached-dominated. The housing here is custom detached hillside houses, mid-century and renovated split-level homes, and newer terraced hillside subdivisions.
SD33's structure is elementary K–5, middle 6–8 and secondary 9–12.

Transit: BC Transit route 57 Broadway runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Young Rd at Olds Dr, Yale Rd at Menzies St and Downtown Chilliwack — service at the downtown/west base of the hill, not on the hill's residential streets.

Anchors off the hill: Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd; the nearest City recreation centres are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way; the nearest grocery named by the City is Save-on-Foods, 46020 Yale Road.
The two "mountains" are different hills in different parts of the city. Little Mountain sits immediately east of downtown; Chilliwack Mountain is across the Fraser River side, west of the core.

Slope, not size, decides what a lot can do. In the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises with the slope band (360 m² up to 990 m²), and DPA 5 captures every City lot at 20% slope or more — two lots of identical area on this hill can carry very different subdivision and building rights.

A geotechnical report is a standard cost here, not an exception. DPA 2 requires one from a qualified professional with each application — budget for the report and the permit before assuming a build, addition or subdivision timeline on any hillside lot.

The elementary school is on the hill; everything else is below it. Little Mountain Elementary (9900 Carleton Street) is the only one of the four named schools physically on the hill — Strathcona Elementary, Chilliwack Middle and Chilliwack Secondary all sit at or below the west base, which shapes the daily trip for middle and secondary students.

The board name and the local name do not fully agree. The one townhouse complex on the hill, Little Mountain Meadows on Quarry Road, is filed in listings under the board sub-area "Chilliwack Proper East" — a buyer searching only the "Little Mountain" sub-area can miss stock that sits on the hill, and vice versa.

The tax penalty clock has two dates, not one. Chilliwack adds 5% after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 4, 2026, and charges drainage and dyking levies on top of municipal rates — a different structure from Mission's flat 10% across the river.

blocks.text: DISTINCTION: Little Mountain is not Chilliwack Mountain. Little Mountain is the smaller hill immediately east of downtown, anchored by Little Mountain Elementary at 9900 Carleton Street; Chilliwack Mountain is a separate community south of the Fraser River, west of downtown. Nothing from Chilliwack Mountain is used here.
Little Mountain Meadows — 9855 Quarry Road. Freehold strata (Strata Plan LMS1998)

A current listing record records: sub-type Townhouse, style Rancher/Bungalow, Title to Land "Freehold – Strata," legal description citing Strata Plan LMS1998, frame-wood construction with vinyl siding, amenities including clubhouse, maintenance grounds and management, and bylaw restrictions recorded as cats OK, dogs OK, number limit two, with restrictions (listing data — confirm on the Form B).
Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Schools (Ministry-listed names only): Little Mountain Elementary (K–5), 9900 Carleton Street, is physically on the hill; Strathcona Elementary (K–5), 46375 Strathcona Road, is at the west side; Chilliwack Middle School (6–8), 46354 Yale Road, and Chilliwack Secondary (9–12), 46363 Yale Road, are in the downtown core below the hill.

Anchors: Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd; Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way, are outside the area.

The board map and the hill disagree (2026-11-01): the only townhouse complex physically on Little Mountain is carried in MLS under a different sub-area name (Chilliwack Proper East) — a buyer searching only "Little Mountain townhouses" can miss the area's entire known townhouse stock.

The hill's two attached products are opposite tenures of attention: Little Mountain Meadows (strata townhouses, no age restriction) and Braeside Estates (bare-land strata detached ranchers, 55+, gated) sit on the same road, Quarry Road — portal summaries routinely blur strata-townhouse, bare-land strata and detached product into one "attached" bucket.

Slope, not lot area, sets the subdivision math: in the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises with the slope band (360 m² to 990 m²), and HR requires 0.2–0.4 ha — a large hillside lot beside a townhouse complex may not subdivide the way its area suggests.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Little Mountain

items.t: Braeside Estates — 9921 Quarry Road.: A current listing describes a gated bare-land strata ("you own your own LOT") of detached ranchers, built 1995 — the buyer owns a strata lot and a detached house, not a townhouse unit and not a fee-simple lot. The listing describes the complex as 55+; a 55+ age bylaw is the only age bylaw form BC law still permits.

Fee-simple hillside lots — the default land form: The documented stock is custom detached hillside houses on view lots, split-level homes and terraced hillside subdivisions — fee-simple lots bought and sold with the house on them; no bare fee-simple lot subdivision is sold as a named product here.

Lot sizes and zones: the hillside residential zones in Zoning Bylaw 2020 No. 5000 include the HR (Hillside Residential) Zone — minimum lot area 0.2 ha where served by a community water system and 0.4 ha for all other uses, minimum lot width 25 m — and the SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) Zone, whose minimum lot area is set by the zone's slope table, starting at 360 m² for the lowest slope band and rising to 990 m² for the highest.
A freehold strata townhouse complex (Rancher/Bungalow form, clubhouse amenity, listing-stated no age restrictions) — built form, not bare land.

Strata vs freehold split: The position is narrower: fee-simple detached lots are the base, Braeside Estates is the one bare-land strata, and Little Mountain Meadows is the one (built) strata townhouse complex.

Hazard character of the land: the hill itself is upland; the City's floodplain framework (Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 — setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River, 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal) matters for base-of-hill and Hope River-side lots rather than the hilltop.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. Nearby areas: downtown Chilliwack to the west, Fairfield Island across the Hope River side to the north, East Chilliwack to the east and southeast.

Little Mountain is not Chilliwack Mountain: Chilliwack Mountain is a separate hillside community on the south side of the Fraser River, west of the downtown core; Little Mountain is the smaller hill immediately east of downtown, anchored by Little Mountain Elementary at 9900 Carleton Street.

Plan frame: the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, is the City's current city-wide plan, and its Development Permit Areas are administered by the City's Land Development Department.

Transit and services: BC Transit route 57 Broadway runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall via Yale Road — service at the downtown/west base of the hill, not on the hill's residential streets. The nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; the nearest hospital is Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd.

Hillside development rules — the central rules for this area: the City's Development Permit Area 2 (Hillside and Upland Areas) protects developments from hazardous hillside conditions and environmentally sensitive areas, and a Geotechnical Report from a qualified professional is required with each application; Development Permit Area 5 (Hillside Development) applies to all lands in the City with slopes of 20% or more, and within a designated DPA a Development Permit is required before subdivision, construction, addition or alteration of a building, or alteration of land, except where exemptions apply. Budget for the report and the permit before assuming a build, addition or subdivision timeline on any hillside lot — fee-simple or bare-land strata.

ALR block, governing no known hill stock: if a parcel were in the ALR, subdivision would require Agricultural Land Commission approval and residences could not be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)); residence caps would be one principal residence per parcel (maximum 500 m²), a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, and one additional residence capped at 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) / 186 m² (over 40 ha); farm class would run in the full three-tier form ($2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31).

The hill's two Quarry Road strata are opposite forms. Braeside Estates (9921 Quarry Rd) is a bare-land strata of detached ranchers — a lot purchase — while Little Mountain Meadows (9855 Quarry Rd) is a built strata townhouse complex — a unit purchase. Portal summaries routinely blur bare-land strata, strata-townhouse and detached product into one "attached" bucket; on this road the distinction is the whole purchase.

The board name and the local name do not fully agree. The hill's known townhouse complex is filed in listings under the board sub-area "Chilliwack Proper East" — a buyer searching only the "Little Mountain" sub-area can miss stock that sits on the hill, and a land buyer should search by address and strata plan, not by sub-area label alone.

Slope is a permit trigger, not just a view feature. At 20% slope or more, DPA 5 applies city-wide and DPA 2 requires a Geotechnical Report with each application — a vacant hillside lot's build timeline starts with a geotechnical budget line that valley-floor lots do not carry.

faq.a: No. Little Mountain is the smaller hillside immediately east of downtown Chilliwack, anchored by Little Mountain Elementary (9900 Carleton Street); Chilliwack Mountain is a separate hillside community on the south side of the Fraser River, west of the downtown core. Nothing from Chilliwack Mountain — listings, schools, hazards — transfers to this hill.
faq.q: Is Little Mountain the same as Chilliwack Mountain?

faq.a: The confirmed strata product by name is one townhouse complex, Little Mountain Meadows (9855 Quarry Road, built 1995); the rest of the confirmed stock is detached hillside housing.
faq.q: Are there any apartment condos on Little Mountain?

faq.a: Development Permit Area 2 (Hillside and Upland) requires a Geotechnical Report from a qualified professional with each application, and Development Permit Area 5 applies to all City lands with slopes of 20% or more; a Development Permit is required before subdivision, construction or land alteration in a designated area, except where exemptions apply.
faq.q: What hillside rules apply to building or subdividing here?

faq.a: The zones set the floor, not the market: HR (Hillside Residential) requires at least 0.2 ha with community water (0.4 ha otherwise) and 25 m width, while SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) runs on a slope table from 360 m² to 990 m² — a "big" hillside lot may not subdivide the way its area suggests.

The confirmed service is at the base: BC Transit route 57 Broadway runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall via Yale Road at Menzies Street and Young Road at Olds Drive; no stop on the hill's residential streets was confirmed, so hilltop homes are a walk or drive from the stop.
faq.q: Is there bus service on Little Mountain?

faq.a: One verified: Little Mountain Meadows, 9855 Quarry Road, a freehold strata townhouse complex (Strata Plan LMS1998). Everything else verified on the hill is detached houses.
faq.q: Is there actually a townhouse complex on Little Mountain?

faq.a: Strata. Title to Land is recorded as Freehold – Strata, so there are strata fees, bylaws, a Form B and a depreciation-report regime — "freehold strata" is not fee-simple ownership.
Listing data records cats OK, dogs OK, number limit two, with restrictions — listing data only; the registered bylaws in the Form B package govern.
The one bare-land strata community documented here, Braeside Estates (9921 Quarry Rd), is own-land strata — you buy the lot and the home, not a pad.
faq.q: Is there a mobile home park on Little Mountain?

faq.a: Yes — on the listing record, Braeside is a bare-land strata ("you own your own LOT"): the purchase is a strata lot plus the detached home on it, with Form B diligence, strata fees and registered bylaws — not an MHPTA pad tenancy.
faq.q: At Braeside, do I own the land?

faq.a: Only a registered 55+ bylaw (valid since Nov 24, 2022 under SPA ss.123.1/123.2) read on the Form B / plan settles it. Do not write an offer around the label until the bylaws are read.

No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA. Plainly, a home on a rented pad is not land ownership.
faq.q: If I buy a pad home elsewhere in Chilliwack instead, do I own the land?
